summary:
Same-sex marriage has been legal nationwide since 2013, the age of consent does not vary with sexual orientation, and a federal anti-discrimination framework applies throughout the country. The Supreme Federal Court ruled in 2018 that legal gender recognition does not require surgery. In 2019 the same court held that constitutional and federal criminal provisions prohibit discrimination and hate crimes on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity, with transphobia punishable on the same footing as racism. Outright International's March 2026 country review records that LGBTIQ people nonetheless continue to face significant violence and discrimination in practice.

Passports and identity cards allow an unspecified or X gender marker under ICAO standards, and state-issued identity cards have been required to offer it since 11 January 2024. A 2025 decision of the Superior Court of Justice permitting a neutral gender entry on the civil registry binds only the plaintiff, though it is treated as a precedent.

Spousal-visa equality and the gender-marker rules apply nationwide, and a marriage recognised in Brazil is recognised for immigration purposes. Partners in registered stable unions are recognised as dependents on health plans and insurers.

The public health system provides sex reassignment surgery free of charge as a matter of constitutional right, following a 2007 ruling by the 4th Regional Federal Court; roughly 250 such operations were performed between 2000 and 2007 at three university hospitals. Access is constrained in practice: the Health Ministry left qualification decisions to local officials, and long waiting lines and poorly equipped public facilities push those who can afford it into private hospitals and clinics. In July 2026 the 3rd Panel of the Superior Court of Justice ruled that health insurance plans must cover facial feminisation surgery, and in March 2024 the Supreme Federal Court extended five-day paid paternity leave to the non-pregnant mothers of lesbian couples.

Adult access to surgery within the public system requires a patient to be at least 21, to carry no diagnosis of personality disorder, and to complete at least two years of psychological evaluation.

Gender-affirming care for minors was banned by the Federal Council of Medicine in April 2025, in the same resolution that lowered the minimum age for gender-affirming surgery from 25 to 21. Advocates filed a Direct Action of Unconstitutionality at the Supreme Federal Court. The Federal Court of Acre blocked the resolution on 25 July 2025, restoring care for minors nationwide; on 2 October 2025 Flávio Dino overturned that block and reinstated the ban. Continuity of medication for trans adolescents, and travel across state lines to obtain care, remain live issues.

Custody placement for LGBTI people who are arrested or imprisoned is governed nationally by National Council of Justice Resolution 348 of 13 October 2020, as amended by Resolution 366 of 20 January 2021. A person is recognised as LGBTI for these purposes by self-declaration before a judge, including at a custody hearing. On arrest, the place of deprivation of liberty is fixed by a judge in a reasoned decision after the person is consulted about their preference; the judge must inform them of the available male, female and LGBTI-specific units and ask trans, travesti and intersex people whether they prefer custody in a female, male or specific unit, and within it the general population or specific wings or cells. The declared preference is recorded, a later change of placement is possible, and transfers are prioritised in cases of violence or serious threat. LGBTI-specific living spaces may not be used as disciplinary isolation, and compulsory transfer as punishment is prohibited. The resolution entered into force after publication, 120 days later, extended to 180 days by Resolution 366/2021.

Practice diverges from the national norm. A peer-reviewed census study of travestis and transgender women in the Rio de Janeiro state prison system interviewed 138 self-declared travesti or trans-woman inmates across eleven units classified as masculine in the metropolitan region between April and June 2021, drawing on the state prison administration's own database. It documents that travestis and trans women in that system are housed in units treated as masculine, with some held in so-called neutral or security units, and characterises placement in male units as a double punishment compounded by recurring violations of basic rights. A 2015 Rio de Janeiro state law grants them parity of treatment with cisgender women in women's units, covering hair length, feminine clothing, accessories and cosmetics.

Violence and hostility directed at trans people are documented. An investigation published in May 2024 found that drink-spiking robberies known locally as 'boa noite, Cinderela' victimise LGBTQIA+ people in São Paulo, as the city prepared for a Pride event drawing thousands of tourists. In October 2024 nearly 1,000 transgender candidates stood in municipal elections across every state amid threats and intimidation; the number of trans officeholders has tripled since the previous cycle.

Courts have applied the anti-discrimination framework to commercial conduct. The 27th Private Chamber of the São Paulo Court of Justice upheld a moral-damage award against a nightclub that refused entry to a trans woman wearing women's clothing; the first-instance decision in Barra Bonita had ordered R$4,000 in compensation. Lower courts pushed the Superior Court of Justice to extend the Maria da Penha Law and the Feminicide Law to trans women, which it did unanimously. The São Paulo Municipal Council's parliamentary inquiry into violence against trans and travesti persons issued a final report carrying 189 recommendations.
tangentialFactors:
Brazil was the first country in Latin America to extend immigration benefits to same-sex partners. On 25 November 2003 Judge Ana Carolina Morozowski of the 5th Civil Court of Curitiba granted permanent residency to the British partner of gay activist Toni Reis, and a week later the National Immigration Council issued Administrative Resolution No. 3 granting temporary or permanent visas to partners without distinction of sex. The government was slow to cable consulates, leaving binational couples confused about how to apply; Immigration Equality and the Brazilian Rainbow Group met officials at the New York consulate in February 2004 to press for clarity. A Florianópolis judge separately barred immigration authorities from deporting an Italian woman partnered with a Brazilian lesbian.

Conversion therapy has been prohibited by the Federal Psychology Council since 1999. A Brasília federal judge approved it in September 2017 and reversed course in December 2017; the Supreme Federal Court ultimately banned the practice, and in 2019 Justice Cármen Lúcia issued an injunction overturning the judge's decisions. Blood donation restrictions on gay and bisexual men, which required 12 months without same-sex activity, were struck down as unconstitutional by the Federal Supreme Court in May 2020.

Legislative opposition to the federal anti-discrimination bill was explicit. Senator Marcelo Crivella argued that homosexuals would receive a protection that 'should have been given to women, the elderly and children', while conservative senators framed the law as an aggression on religious freedom. In January 2019 openly gay representative Jean Wyllys left Brazil after death threats and was replaced in February by David Miranda. The Catholic Church and radical evangelical groups have been identified as sources of rising intolerance.
localsOnly:
Trans youth face specific risks. In the central, north and north-eastern regions, transgender people from extremely poor families sometimes begin sex work as early as age 12 after being expelled from home; travestis commonly work the streets from the age of 16 or 17 in the southern and south-eastern regions and in major capitals.

Schools are a contested area. In June 2024 the Supreme Federal Court ruled that public and private schools must combat discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, sexist bullying against cisgender and transgender girls, and homotransphobic bullying. Since 2020 the Court has been overturning state and municipal laws banning gender and sexuality courses in schools, and since 2023 it has been overturning laws banning gender-neutral language in schools. A 2004 government initiative, Brasil Sem Homophobia, was designed to protect LGBTQ students.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 2025 Superior Court of Justice decision allowing a neutral gender entry on the civil registry was decided for the individual plaintiff; its effect on other applicants is not established.

Litigation over the Federal Council of Medicine's April 2025 resolution is unresolved. The Direct Action of Unconstitutionality remains pending, and the lower-court block and its reversal leave the position of trans adolescents uncertain.

The prison census covering travestis and transgender women is limited to the Rio de Janeiro state system and does not establish conditions in other states.

No trans-specific entry or airport screening practice is documented in the source inventory, and no trans-disaggregated homicide data with a comparable denominator is sourced.
